data.one_liner: Displays customizable sliding and popup toasts with animations, queueing, and stacking modes.
data.what_it_does: Allows developers to display customizable sliding and popup toast notifications with features like tap actions, animation controls, drag-to-dismiss, and queueing/stacking behavior. It supports rich styling, custom leading/trailing widgets, and long-message dialog triggers.
use_when: You need customizable sliding or popup toast notifications in your Flutter app.
You require advanced toast queueing modes like one-by-one or stacked notifications.
You want users to be able to tap toasts to view long messages inside a dialog.
avoid_when: You need system-level push notifications or local OS notifications.
Your project relies on an older version of Flutter prior to 3.47.0.
strengths: Supports multiple display modes including all-at-once, one-by-one queueing, and notification-style stacking.
Rich customization options for layout, alignment, animations, styling, and glassmorphism.
Built-in accessibility/utility features like long-press to pause and tap-to-read dialogs.
weaknesses: Requires a relatively recent Flutter version (3.47.0 and newer).
Not suited for persistent local push notifications.
data.setup_notes: Requires Flutter 3.47.0 and Dart 3.13.0 or newer. Simply add the dependency to pubspec.yaml.

alternatives.name: fluttertoast
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a lightweight, simple toast package that natively bridges platform toasts.

alternatives.name: toastification
alternatives.why_pick_it: For a highly stylized toast library with rich built-in themes and progress indicators.

alternatives.name: bot_toast
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a highly extensible overlay management system that can show toasts, loading indicators, and custom dialogs anywhere.
